name: Robot Arm
desc: A pedestal-mounted articulated arm working a pick-and-place programme — analytic inverse kinematics fold the machined links to every waypoint, the base yaws so the whole rig foreshortens, the gripper closes on a hatched blank and lets it go again, and live joint-angle callouts count the degrees off a dashed work envelope.

energy.doc: programme rate + link weight + tool glow + sway

scale.doc: arm height vs frame — 1 stands about half the short edge

density.doc: how many waypoints in the programme (4..9)

speed.doc: how fast it works through the programme

y.doc: the foot of the pedestal, canvas fraction

reach.doc: how far out the programme sends the tool — 1 works the arm to full stretch

anno.doc: annotation density: work envelope, TCP locus, joint callouts, readout

style.doc: aesthetic: toned drafting film / prussian cyanotype / aged engraved plate / additive x-ray ghost / kinematic (links collapse to a bare stick chain with joint axes)

seed.doc: the waypoint programme: positions, yaws, tool angles, grip pattern

alpha.doc: opacity — the arm is line work over open ground, so it layers politely
